title: Indefinido and imperfecto together
goal: Choose between a completed event and the background in one story.
theory: In a story `imperfecto` sets the background and `indefinido` moves the plot on: `Era de noche y llovía cuando llegué a casa.` Imperfecto describes setting, age, weather, habit; indefinido names a completed event: `Entré, encendí la luz y me senté.` If an action was in progress when another happened, use `estaba` + gerund: `Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.` Some verbs change meaning: `Conocí a Ana en 2010` (I met her), `Conocía a Ana` (I knew her).

title: Pluscuamperfecto: what happened earlier
goal: Say that one action in the past happened before another.
theory: `Pluscuamperfecto` = `había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían` + participle: `había trabajado`, `habías comido`. It shows that an action was finished before another action in the past: `Cuando llegué, ya se había ido.` It often goes with `ya`, `todavía no`, `nunca`: `Nunca había visto el mar.` The irregular participles are the same: `hecho`, `dicho`, `visto`, `escrito`, `puesto`, `vuelto`.

title: Futuro simple: will be and probably is
goal: Talk about the future and about guesses in the present.
theory: Add the endings `-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án` to the infinitive: `hablaré`, `comerás`, `vivirá`. Some verbs have a special stem: `tener → tendré`, `hacer → haré`, `poder → podré`, `salir → saldré`, `decir → diré`, `venir → vendré`. The futuro speaks about the future and about a guess in the present: `Serán las ocho` — it must be about eight o'clock. The spoken future is `ir a`: `Voy a salir`. For promises and forecasts use the futuro: `Mañana lloverá.`

title: Condicional: I would, a polite request
goal: Give advice, ask politely and speak about an unreal wish.
theory: Add the endings `-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían` to the infinitive: `hablaría`, `comería`, `viviría`. The special stems are the same as in the futuro: `tendría`, `haría`, `podría`, `saldría`, `diría`. The condicional is used for a polite request (`¿Podría ayudarme?`), advice (`Deberías descansar`), a wish (`Me gustaría viajar`) and a guess about the past (`Serían las ocho`). In reported speech the future becomes the condicional: `Dijo que vendría`.

title: Two pronouns together: se lo doy
goal: Put the indirect and the direct object next to each other.
theory: The order is always the same: indirect first, then direct: `Me lo da`, `Te la envío`. If both pronouns are third person, `le/les` becomes `se`: `Le doy el libro → Se lo doy.` You cannot say `le lo`. Pronouns go before the conjugated verb, and with an infinitive, gerund and imperative they are attached: `Dámelo`, `Voy a dárselo`, `Estoy escribiéndotela`. The direct object is `lo/la`, the indirect is `le`.

title: Imperative: usted, ustedes and with pronouns
goal: Give instructions politely and with pronouns, in the affirmative and the negative.
theory: For polite address use subjunctive forms: `hable`, `coma`, `escriba` (usted) and `hablen`, `coman`, `escriban` (ustedes). For `vosotros` in the affirmative the infinitive changes `-r` into `-d`: `hablad`, `comed`, `escribid`; in the negative use the subjunctive: `no habléis`. With pronouns, in the affirmative they are attached: `Cómpralo`, `Dímelo`, `Siéntese`; in the negative they go before the verb: `No lo compres`, `No me lo digas`. An accent is written to keep the stress.

title: Present subjunctive: the form and when it is needed
goal: Form the present subjunctive and use it after a request, a wish and an emotion.
theory: The form comes from the `yo` form of the present: drop `-o` and change the vowel to the opposite one. `-ar` takes `-e, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en`: `hable`; `-er/-ir` takes `-a, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an`: `coma`, `viva`. Special forms: `ser → sea`, `ir → vaya`, `estar → esté`, `saber → sepa`, `haber → haya`. It is needed after a wish, a request and an emotion when the two clauses have different subjects: `Quiero que vengas.` `Me alegro de que estés aquí.`

title: Subjunctive: wish, probability, emotion
goal: Express a wish, probability and an opinion with the subjunctive.
theory: Wish and request: `Quiero que…`, `Espero que…`, `Prefiero que…`: `Espero que llegues pronto.` Probability: `Quizás`, `tal vez`, `probablemente` + subjunctive: `Quizás vaya.` If you are sure, use the indicative: `Seguramente viene.` Emotion and judgement: `Me gusta que…`, `Es una pena que…`, `Es importante que…`: `Es importante que estudies.` For general judgements with no specific subject use the infinitive: `Es importante estudiar.`

title: Relative words: que, quien, donde
goal: Join two sentences with que, quien, donde, cuyo.
theory: `Que` is the most common relative word: `El libro que leo es interesante.` After a preposition put an article before it: `la casa en la que vivo`, `el chico con el que hablas`. For people you can use `quien`: `La chica con quien hablas`. `Donde` is place: `La ciudad donde nací`. `Cuyo` means "whose" and agrees with what is owned: `El hombre cuya hija vive aquí`. If the thing sought is unknown or does not exist, use the subjunctive: `Busco una casa que tenga jardín.`

title: Periphrases: tener que, acabar de, soler
goal: Express obligation, habit, beginning and end of an action with periphrases.
theory: A periphrasis is a conjugated verb plus a non-finite form. Obligation: `tener que` + infinitive (`Tengo que estudiar`), `hay que` + infinitive (`Hay que descansar`), `deber` + infinitive. Habit: `soler` + infinitive (`Suelo comer en casa`). Beginning and end: `empezar a`, `ponerse a`, `acabar de` (have just), `dejar de`: `Acabo de llegar.` `He dejado de fumar.` Continuing: `seguir` + gerund: `Sigo trabajando.` Repeating: `volver a` + infinitive: `Vuelvo a llamar.`

title: Gerund and participle in a sentence
goal: Use the gerund for manner and the participle as an adjective.
theory: The gerund shows how, or at the same time as what, an action happens: `Aprendo español leyendo.` `Entró cantando.` It does not change and does not come after a preposition (use the infinitive instead): `antes de salir`. The participle `-ado/-ido` does not change in compound tenses: `He comido`. As an adjective it agrees: `la puerta cerrada`, `los libros escritos`. With `estar` it shows a result: `La tienda está cerrada.`

title: Conjunctions and clauses: porque, cuando, para que
goal: Join sentences with reason, time, purpose and concession.
theory: Reason: `porque`, `como`, `puesto que`: `Como llueve, me quedo.` Purpose: `para` + infinitive (same subject) or `para que` + subjunctive (different subjects): `Estudio para aprobar.` `Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.` Time: `cuando`, `antes de que`, `después de que`; about the future `cuando` needs the subjunctive: `Cuando llegues, llámame.` Concession: `aunque`, `a pesar de que`. Result: `por eso`, `así que`.

title: Adverbs: manner, time and frequency
goal: Use adverbs in -mente and adverbs of time and frequency.
theory: Adverbs in `-mente` are formed from the feminine form of the adjective: `rápida → rápidamente`, `fácil → fácilmente`. If there are two in a row, only the last takes `-mente`: `rápida y claramente`. Time and frequency: `ya`, `todavía`, `aún`, `siempre`, `nunca`, `a veces`, `de vez en cuando`. Quantity: `muy`, `mucho`, `bastante`, `demasiado`. `Muy` goes before an adjective and adverb: `muy bien`; `mucho` goes after a verb: `trabajo mucho`. Before `mejor`, `peor` use `mucho`: `mucho mejor`.

title: Health and how you feel
goal: Tell a doctor what hurts and understand simple advice.
theory: To speak about pain use `doler`: `Me duele la cabeza.` `Me duelen los pies.` A doctor may ask: `¿Qué le pasa?` `¿Desde cuándo?` Advice: `Debe descansar.` `Tiene que tomar este medicamento.` Useful words: `la fiebre`, `la receta`, `el dolor`, `el resfriado`.

title: Travel and hotels
goal: Book a room, buy a ticket and deal with a problem on a trip.
theory: On a trip request formulas are useful: `Quería reservar una habitación.` `¿Tiene alguna habitación libre?` `¿Cuánto cuesta la noche?` Tickets: `un billete de ida y vuelta`. Problems: `He perdido…`, `Se ha estropeado…`. Words: `la reserva`, `el equipaje`, `el vuelo`, `la llegada`, `la salida`.

title: Opinions and feelings
goal: Give an opinion, agree or object.
theory: To give an opinion: `Creo que…`, `Me parece que…`, `En mi opinión…`. After `creo que` the indicative: `Creo que es bueno`; after `no creo que` the subjunctive: `No creo que sea bueno.` Agreement: `Estoy de acuerdo`, `Tienes razón`. Objection: `No estoy de acuerdo`, `Eso no es verdad`.

title: Reading a short article
goal: Understand the topic of an article, its main ideas and the author's attitude.
theory: When you read an article, first read the headline and the first paragraph, then find the key words. Do not try to translate every word. Notice the linking words: `sin embargo` (however), `por eso` (that is why), `además` (besides), `en cambio` (on the other hand). They show how ideas are connected.

title: Reading instructions and rules
goal: Understand instructions and rules and find prohibitions and obligations.
theory: In instructions look for verbs of command and prohibition: `Pulse`, `No abra`, `Debe`. Impersonal forms are common: `Se prohíbe fumar`, `Se ruega silencio`. Numbers and order mark the steps: `1.º`, `2.º`, `primero`, `después`, `por último`. Read to the end: the prohibition is often at the end.

title: Writing a letter: a request and a complaint
goal: Write a letter with a request or a complaint and state the point politely.
theory: A formal letter has a greeting, a purpose, details, a request and a closing. A model: `Estimados señores: Les escribo para… Les agradecería que… Atentamente, Ana García.` For a request use `¿Podría…?`, `Le agradecería que` + subjunctive. Write short sentences and avoid colloquial words.

title: Listening to radio and news
goal: Understand the main topic of a short report and the main facts.
theory: News is spoken faster. First get the topic, then the details: who, what, where, when. Listen for numbers and place names. Do not stop at unknown words: the meaning is often clear from context. Key words: `según`, `fuentes`, `ayer`, `hoy`.

title: Listening to a conversation about past events
goal: Understand what happened and in what order in an everyday story.
theory: In stories about the past listen to the verbs: `fui`, `llegué` are events; `era`, `estaba` are background. Follow the order words: `primero`, `luego`, `después`, `al final`. Write the sequence of events in brief notes, then retell it.

title: Speaking: giving an opinion
goal: Give an opinion and support it with arguments.
theory: It is handy to build an opinion like this: position, reason, example. `Creo que es una buena idea porque ahorramos tiempo. Por ejemplo, ...` To object: `Entiendo, pero…`. Do not be afraid of a pause: use linking words `bueno`, `pues`, `a ver`.

title: Speaking: telling about a trip
goal: Tell about a trip or an event from the past in a connected way.
theory: A story about a trip: where, with whom, what you did, what you liked. `El año pasado fui a Italia con mi hermana. Visitamos Roma y Florencia. Lo que más me gustó fue…` Use indefinido for events and imperfecto for description: `Hacía sol y la ciudad era preciosa.` Speak aloud following a plan.
